records.name: Caribbean Festival and Cultural Organization of Pennsylvania Inc.
records.summary: Runs a free, family festival each August celebrating Caribbean culture with music, food, fashion and vendors, staffed by volunteers.
records.what_you_do: Attend the festival, volunteer on festival day through the volunteer page, or apply for the vendor booth or scholarship listed on the site.

schedule.text: Free festival each August, on a Sunday from noon to 8 pm

first_step.how: Come to the August Sunday festival at Cherry Street Pier, or email the organizers to ask about volunteering
first_step.basis: The festival is free and open to all, and the site invites new volunteers to get involved and lists a contact email and phone
first_step.what_to_expect: The festival runs from noon to 8 pm on the pier, with music, food, fashion and vendor booths. Anyone can walk in for free. The committee members who plan it are unpaid volunteers.
first_visit_tips: Plan your ride, since the pier is reachable by public transit
Street parking is available nearby, paid and free, so allow time to find a spot
Email or call ahead if you want to volunteer on festival day

records.notes: Site lists a second general number, (215) 879-9352, which is not in our record. Some older page text mentions a 2024 Penn's Landing event; 2026 details (Aug 16, 2026, Cherry Street Pier) were used. The site gives no accessibility, language or volunteer sign-up details, so those are left out. Vendor page: phillycaribbeanfestival.com/vendors/vendor-applications/. Scholarship application: phillycaribbeanfestival.com/scholarship-application/.

records.name: Cleaver Magazine
records.summary: An independent online literary magazine, published quarterly since 2013, that also runs writing classes and needs volunteer reviewers, editors and interns.
records.what_you_do: Take a live online writing class, volunteer as a reviewer, editor or intern, or send in writing through its online submissions portal.

schedule.text: Live online classes run on set dates and times, most about two hours. Some classes are 90 minutes.

cost.text: The quarterly magazine is free to subscribe to. Most classes cost $60, one bundle costs $100, and some sessions are pay what you want.

first_step.how: Pick a live class on the Classes page and register through its link, or subscribe to the free quarterly issue first
first_step.basis: Classes are open to writers of all genres and experience levels and can be booked online, but some expect a draft you bring to class, and each class has a seat limit
first_step.what_to_expect: Classes are live on Zoom with a set date and time, usually about two hours. Seats are limited, from 4 to 25 people depending on the class. Some classes ask you to bring a short draft of up to 1,000 words, and some sessions are not recorded.
first_visit_tips: Read the class description to see whether you need to bring a draft
Register early, since small classes fill up

records.notes: Volunteer roles (reviewer, editor, intern) are listed, but the opportunities page does not say how to apply, what time it takes, or where it happens. Class registration runs through the magazine's submissions site. Location is online only as far as the pages show.

records.name: CraftNOW Philadelphia
records.summary: An organization that supports the craft community of Philadelphia. It runs CraftMONTH each November, with free hands-on craft activities, a symposium, citywide exhibitions, and education for kids, teens and adults.
records.what_you_do: Take part in the free CraftNOW Create activities or the symposium during CraftMONTH, sign up for the mailing list, or join the education programs for kids, teens or adults.

schedule.text: CraftMONTH runs each November, with free hands-on activities, a day-long symposium and craft exhibitions across the city through December.

cost.text: The symposium is free. CraftMONTH activities on the site are listed as free.

first_step.how: Sign up for the mailing list on the home page, then pick a free CraftMONTH event in November 2026, such as the November 12 symposium
first_step.basis: Events are free and open to the public with dates listed, and the site has a mailing list sign-up. The site does not say how to register for each activity.
first_step.what_to_expect: CraftNOW Create offers demonstrations and hands-on craft activities for people of many ages. The symposium is a free day of talks on Philadelphia craft history and artists, held in person at Moore College of Art and Design and online. Exhibitions run at craft shows across the city through December.
first_visit_tips: Check the events list for exact 2026 dates and times before you go
The symposium can be joined online, which helps if travel is hard

records.notes: The 2026 CraftNOW Create date is unclear on the site (Nov 7 and Nov 2 both appear), so no date is given. The CraftNOW Create page also describes a 2024 event at Smith Memorial Playground, which is not used as a schedule. The 2026 symposium date (Thursday, November 12, 2026) is on the symposium page. The adults education page lists many other craft studios across the city; those are businesses and were not recorded here. No accessibility details were found on the site. Kids, teens and adult education pages exist but describe no dates or prices.

records.name: Elfreth's Alley Association, Inc
records.summary: Keeps Elfreth's Alley and its history in view. The association runs a small museum in two of the Alley's houses, leads guided tours, and holds events such as a fall makers market and a December holiday event.
records.what_you_do: Volunteers greet visitors and share Alley history, help run events like the makers market and Deck the Alley, or do project work such as garden upkeep, building care, and archives. Anyone can visit the museum or join a guided tour.

schedule.text: Museum open Friday to Sunday, noon to 4 pm. Guided tours Saturday and Sunday at 2:30 pm, about 40 minutes. Volunteers can come weekly, monthly, or only for major events.

cost.text: Museum: $3 for adults and $2 for children 7 to 12. Guided tour: $10 for adults and $5 for children 7 to 12, museum included. Audio tour: $3. Tickets are sold in person only, by cash, card or Apple Pay.

first_step.how: Visit the museum or join a 2:30 pm Saturday or Sunday guided tour, or fill out the volunteer interest form on the Volunteer with Us page
first_step.basis: The volunteer page says no history background is needed, training is provided, and new volunteers get a packet of common questions. Visits and tours need no sign-up.
first_step.what_to_expect: A tour lasts about 40 minutes with an expert guide, and it covers the full length of the Alley and Bladen's Court, with entry to both museum houses. Tickets are bought in person, so plan to pay at the door. Volunteers mostly greet visitors, share Alley history, help at events, or work on garden, building or archive projects.
first_visit_tips: Tours start at 2:30 pm on weekends, so arrive a few minutes early
Bring cash or a card, since online ticketing is not offered
Ask the museum about stairs and access before you go, because the site does not cover it

records.notes: Upcoming dated items on the homepage (October haunted history show and a November 7 makers market) are not in the schedule text. The volunteer page does not mention a background check or minimum age, and the site has no accessibility or transit details.

records.name: Feminist Bird Club Philly
records.summary: The Philadelphia chapter of a national birding group that makes room for women, LGBTQIA+ people and people of color. Members go on bird walks and outings together and share news through a newsletter.
records.what_you_do: Go on guided bird walks, identify birds with others, and sign up for outings through the chapter's link page.

schedule.text: Outings come up through the year, often on Saturday mornings, and each one has its own sign-up form.

locations.label: Philadelphia parks, such as Tacony Creek Park, Awbury Arboretum and the Strawberry Mansion Reservoir area

cost.text: Not stated on the chapter pages. Past Awbury Arboretum hikes were listed as free.

first_step.how: Fill in the sign-up form for an upcoming outing on the chapter's Linktree page, and sign up for the newsletter there
first_step.basis: Outings are open to the public through a sign-up form, but the chapter pages do not say what a first walk is like.

records.notes: The latest listed outing is a Saturday, 10/10 trip to Palmyra Cove in New Jersey (the Linktree page does not show the year; Oct 10 is a Saturday in 2026). Philadelphia outings are announced on the Instagram account, and the national events page has no Philadelphia dates. Nothing on the site says whether a first walk needs binoculars or experience. The national chapter list links only to the Instagram account for Philly.

records.name: First Unitarian Church of Philadelphia
records.summary: A Unitarian Universalist congregation on Chestnut Street. It holds Sunday services in person and on Zoom, and has a New Here path for visitors.
records.what_you_do: Attend a Sunday service, join the 20s and 30s group, or take part in adult spirit and learning programs.

schedule.text: Sunday worship at 11 am, in person and on Zoom.

cost.text: Not listed on the pages checked

access.notes: The first floor, including the Sanctuary and Parish Room, is wheelchair accessible, with wheelchair seating in the Sanctuary. A temporary ramp at the Van Pelt Street entrance was installed in 2023. The Sanctuary has a hearing loop for hearing aid users. The site does not say about an elevator, ASL, captioning or a quiet room.

first_step.how: Come to Sunday worship at 11 am, in person or on Zoom, and fill out the new visitor card if you like; stay for coffee hour afterward
first_step.basis: The New Here page explains a first visit, offers a visitor card and coffee hour to meet members, and describes Pathway to Membership sessions for newcomers.
first_step.what_to_expect: Sunday worship starts at 11 am, in person or on Zoom. Afterward you can stay for coffee hour to meet members. The congregation has more than 250 members, and newcomers can take part in Pathway to Membership sessions to learn about its history and beliefs.
first_visit_tips: Check the Getting Here page for directions before you come
If you prefer, join the Zoom service from home

records.notes: The site has a 20s and 30s group page (philauu.org/young-adults/) and a Children and Youth page, which were not read in depth. The New Here page does not state the service length, dress, or cost of membership. A search for worship details surfaced church bulletins, which were not used as sources.

records.name: Friends of Dickinson Square Park
records.summary: Neighbors who care for John Dickinson Square Park in South Philadelphia. A Tree Team waters young trees each week, a gardening committee tends the park, and a parents' committee works with families.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for a weekly watering shift of about 45 minutes (training is provided), join the gardening committee, or join the parents' committee.

schedule.text: Tree Team watering is a weekly shift of about 45 minutes that you pick to fit your week, signed up through the group's form.

first_step.how: Fill out the Tree Team form on the group's website to pick a weekly watering shift; for the gardening committee, email the contact listed on the site
first_step.basis: The site says training is provided for the watering work and gives a sign-up form for new volunteers, plus an email route for the gardening committee.
first_step.what_to_expect: A Tree Team shift is about 45 minutes once a week, spent watering young trees in the park. You pick a shift that fits your schedule, and training is provided for the work. The parents' committee is a separate family group that also joins through a form.
first_visit_tips: Pick a weekly shift that fits your routine, so it is easy to keep
Join the Facebook group or the newsletter for news about park work

records.notes: The site lists no meeting times, work day dates, park hours, accessibility, transit or parking details. The Tree Team form and the parents' committee form share one link. A newsletter sign-up page exists at friends-of-dickinson-square-park.kit.com but was not read.

notes: Seven groups in batch w6-tier2-deep-a/02 were researched, 16 page fetches and 1 search used, within budget. CraftNOW's adult education page lists many craft studios; they are businesses, so they were not recorded. Cleaver's classes are online only. First Unitarian's search surfaced a bulletin and a third-party listing that were not used as sources beyond the church's own pages. Group status for CraftNOW was left at the tier 1 date (2026-01) because the site shows no dated post.
